The 192–252-bit screen has a real split. Of 537 exact models, 247 pass the necessary cubic-depth test but still need a cover witness; 137 fail that depth test, and 153 fall outside the recorded genus-three domain. Their selected-subgroup advantages remain unmeasured. Open a row to inspect both branch screens.

02 / Recognize

Ten criteria, distinct gates

Use these tests to generate candidates, then follow the listed witness requirements before assigning a stronger grade.

Download criteria JSON ↗

03 / Verify

From a lead to a measured route

Each stage narrows the claim to the exact object and selected subgroup it concerns.

01 / Identity

Fix the model

Record field representation, equation, trace, point count, and a stable model identity. A class result does not identify every model in that class.

02 / Criterion

Check the hypothesis

Compute the trace, factor the selected order, calculate embedding degree, or realize a covering. Preserve exceptional cases and negative results.

03 / Transfer

Certify the map

For pairings and coverings, exhibit a nondegenerate or injective map for the chosen subgroup and target. Record any kernel intersection.

04 / Cost

Measure the work

Include construction and transport costs, then compare a verified target under a matched resource contract.

Exact criterion a checked model and the stated mathematical condition Geometry a positive cover-model signal Candidate an unresolved transfer or cost gate

04 / Provenance

Trace each row back

The curve snapshot is deterministically exported from two source-locked SQLite databases. Three prime-field examples were exhaustively counted in Rust and independently checked in PARI. The criteria link to original papers or the local proof record.
